added_assumptions.label: ass:iid-sampling
added_assumptions.statement: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).

added_assumptions.label: ass:conditional-density-law
added_assumptions.statement: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\).

added_assumptions.label: ass:polynomial-thinning
added_assumptions.statement: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\).

added_assumptions.label: ass:holder-regression
added_assumptions.statement: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a continuous extension \(\mu_x^P\) satisfying \(\left|\mu_x^P(t)-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)(t-s)^j/j!\right|\leq L|t-s|^\beta\) for all \(s,t\in[0,1]\).

proposed_from.topic: Honest minimax risk and confidence-length frontier for noninvertible threshold modified-treatment policies under polynomial generalized-propensity thinning. On the fixed finite-stratum Holder model, prove the exact natural-course-plus-Dirac decomposition, let h solve n h^(2 beta+1)(delta+h)^kappa asymptotic to one, and establish the sharp rate n^(-1/2)+delta^(kappa+1)h^beta with its regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes. Construct a total-Gram-stabilized local-polynomial atom estimator and bias-aware uniformly honest interval attaining the rate for every declared threshold sequence, and prove matching same-class global-shift and localized-Bernoulli lower bounds. Use the official lmtp threshold-policy workflow as consumer and do not smooth or replace the target. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The target equals an observable natural-course mean plus q_x(delta)mu_x(delta), with q_x(delta) asymptotic to delta^(kappa+1). Local information is n h(delta+h)^kappa, so Holder bias-variance balance gives the stated scale. For beta=kappa=1, pi(a)=2a yields h=(n delta)^(-1/3), KL of order n delta h^3, target separation delta^2h, and transition delta=n^(-1/10). Searches found threshold policies explicitly excluded from published LMTP EIF theory although the package accepts user policies. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform realized-design total-Gram lemma, under only two-sided polynomial density bounds, controlling exact local-polynomial l1/l2 weights and the singular-Gram fallback probability tightly enough for honest O(r_n) expected length over all deterministic delta sequences. EARLY KILL TEST: In the one-cell beta=kappa=1 class with arbitrary measurable density c_-a<=pi(a)<=c_+a, prove those weight and bad-event bounds and a finite-sample honest interval of length O(n^-1/2+delta^2h); pivot or stop if propensity smoothness is unavoidable.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level sources are Díaz et al., who prove identification but explicitly exclude continuous threshold policies from root-\(n\) optimality theory, and Gaiffas, who gives the pointwise degenerate-design rate for an unweighted fixed regression value. The proposed functional is neither: it is a regular observed mean plus a shrinking mass times a moving point evaluation under an explicit novel global measurable polynomial treatment-assignment envelope. That composition creates the new critical threshold \(n^{-1/[2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)]}\), which is separated from the local boundary-design scale, and it changes both the lower-bound separation and the cost of singular-Gram fallback. Armstrong and Kolesár do not cover this random thinned design. McCoy et al. correctly define their clipped-policy density ratio relative to an appropriate dominating measure and target the pushforward law directly; their stochastic-shift effect-modifier estimand and high-probability regularity guarantees do not supply the deterministic-clamp moving-threshold minimax risk or uniformly honest expected-length frontier.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; threshold example; Identification Theorem 1; optimality discussion preceding Assumption 4; Efficient Influence Function Theorem 2; weak-convergence theorem.
seed_details.kernel: Exact Lebesgue-plus-Dirac decomposition and matched minimax rate \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) uniformly over a two-sided polynomial density class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the piecewise-invertible change of variables and ordinary density ratio by a mixed-measure pushforward, then estimate its point-mass regression value locally.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for deterministic threshold LMTPs paired with minimax, Dirac, atom, polynomial thinning, or honest confidence length found no result; the closest 2026 clipping paper still imposes a regular density-ratio expansion.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is immediate from Gaiffas because the clamp merely asks for a regression value at \(\delta_n\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The target also has a regular empirical-mean component, the point value is attenuated by an endogenous atom mass, and the moving threshold creates a new critical scale \(\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\) distinct from the boundary-design scale.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate is derived from two matching same-class experiments and an explicit estimator; it is not an analogue on a self-defined oracle class.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; general bias-aware criterion; Theorems 2.1 and 2.2; boundary-point application; Appendix A coverage proof.
seed_details.kernel: A finite-sample bias-aware interval with minimax-order expected length under arbitrary measurable polynomially thinned random designs, using total-Gram stabilization and an atom fallback.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition on the realized local design, control exact intercept weights through an unnormalized Gram event, and integrate the fallback length rather than assuming a regular design sequence.
seed_details.destination_search: The target-method search found fixed-design honest intervals and random-design point estimators, but no interval combining uniform random-Gram tails, atom attenuation, and every deterministic moving threshold.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Armstrong and Kolesár already give honest local-polynomial intervals at boundaries.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their expected-length argument does not absorb singular local Gram events under a density that vanishes and is only bounded between measurable polynomial envelopes.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The inference layer contains its own sharp expected-length lower bound and a named total-Gram object.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; local-polynomial and Lepski construction; conditional Theorem 1; regularly varying Theorem 2; adaptive lower-bound Theorem 3 and Section 7.4 proof; discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the exact honest adaptation penalty when both \(\beta\) and \(\kappa\) are unknown and the atom term can be hidden below the regular \(n^{-1/2}\) floor.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Weight the between-class modulus by \(q_x(\delta_n)\) and splice it with the regular mean experiment before applying a Lepski selector.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found logarithmic adaptation for unweighted degenerate-design point estimation and convex-modulus limits for fixed design, but no atom-attenuated clamp functional.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Gaiffas already proves that adaptation costs a logarithm.
seed_details.rebuttal: The shrinking atom can fall below the parametric component, so the logarithmic penalty may disappear on part of the threshold sequence space and must be re-derived from a composite modulus.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for an exact adaptation frontier rather than appending a generic data-driven bandwidth.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Software-paper workflow and user-policy specification, read together with the theoretical-requirements appendix of Hoffman et al. and the current package documentation.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the exact object missed by an ordinary post-policy density ratio for a clamp and replace it by a regular-plus-atom estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute the pushforward as a measure before attempting a Radon--Nikodym ratio.
seed_details.destination_search: The package accepts user policy functions, while the tutorial warns that continuous thresholds violate piecewise invertibility; no package-facing atomic correction was found.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The software documentation never promises valid threshold inference, so there is no estimator to correct.
seed_details.rebuttal: The seed is retained only as a consumer-facing decomposition and not as a claim that the package authors proved validity for this input.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The diagnosis is paired with a corrected estimator, a regime characterization, and minimax inference.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; piecewise-invertibility scope paragraph; weak-convergence theorem for the SDR vector; simultaneous-inference construction; discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the mixed Gaussian limit experiment when the empirical natural-course term and the atom-localization term meet at \(\delta_n\asymp\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the stacked EIF central limit theorem by a joint triangular-array expansion with a local-polynomial component and non-negligible Hölder bias.
seed_details.destination_search: No critical-regime limit law was found for an atom-weighted moving point evaluation; standard dose-response CLTs assume ordinary overlap and undersmoothing.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The limit is just a sum of two Gaussian terms.
seed_details.rebuttal: At minimax bandwidth the Hölder bias is first-order and its least-favorable drift, covariance with the retained term, and uniform law are not supplied by a standard CLT.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposed limit object is the local experiment, not an assumed asymptotic normality statement.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction and motivation; threshold-response definition; stochastic-intervention identification; efficient-influence-function theorem; uniform Gaussian-process proof; conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Construct a simultaneous band for the exact clamp curve across threshold values that cross the regular-to-atom transition.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Donsker EIF curve by threshold-dependent total-Gram atom estimators with nonconstant normalization.
seed_details.destination_search: Threshold-response bands found in the search average over the supported region; smooth-LMTP trajectory bands explicitly exclude threshold maps.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is an immediate chaining argument after the pointwise interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: The moving atom location, changing normalization, and singular-Gram events create a nonstationary process whose entropy and bias envelope are not pointwise consequences.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The stochastic region-average comparator is kept distinct from the deterministic clamp target.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Efficient Influence Function Theorem 2, single-time-point reduction, and Weak Convergence Theorem 3.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a triangular-array efficiency bound for sequences on which the atom term is negligible and the clamp mean becomes asymptotically equivalent to a regular observed mean.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project the shrinking atomic derivative onto the root-\(n\) tangent experiment rather than representing it by a fixed density ratio.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for shrinking-weight point evaluation and triangular-array pathwise differentiability found no direct treatment of this functional.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Once the atom term is \(o(n^{-1/2})\), the result is merely efficiency of an observed mean.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the regular regime alone, so this seed was dropped as a standalone efficiency-bound paper and retained only as one branch of the full phase diagram.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M11 efficiency lane was generated as required but rejected because its nontrivial content collapses without the other regimes.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Policy-facing introduction; inverse threshold-response objective; simultaneous band construction; conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a clamp threshold from data and derive regret relative to the best threshold when value estimation crosses the atom frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the root-\(n\) uniform value process by a regime-dependent nonregular modulus before analyzing the empirical maximizer.
seed_details.destination_search: Crippa studies regret for treatment-assignment threshold rules, but not thresholds indexing a modified continuous-treatment clamp; nevertheless the target would change from the fixed LMTP mean requested here.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a standard threshold-policy empirical-welfare problem after inserting a slower value-estimation rate.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nonuniform rate complicates the argmax, but the seed was dropped because the exact fixed-policy target and official workflow are the stated consumer, while threshold selection introduces a different decision problem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The required M16 lane was searched against the named threshold-regret literature and was not relabelled as fixed-estimand estimation.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; convex-modulus construction; optimal one- and two-sided interval theorems; proof by least-favorable normal experiments; adaptation discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Invert a conditional sign or permutation test for the local atom value and combine it with the retained empirical mean.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Supply an exact symmetry orbit conditional on the random local design.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found conformal prediction intervals for future outcomes and bias-aware confidence intervals for regression means, but no exchangeability orbit identifying a Hölder regression mean at one point.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Bounded regression errors need not be symmetric, so there is no exact permutation group for the conditional mean.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds under the declared model; adding symmetry would strengthen the model solely for the method, so the seed was killed rather than padded.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The required M17 lane was rejected because its symmetry assumption is absent from the scientific model.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Longitudinal motivation; recursive Identification Theorem 1; density-ratio EIF Theorem 2; TMLE and SDR weak-convergence theorems; application discussion.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a recursive mixed continuous-atomic representation and minimax rate for repeated clamps at multiple visits.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace each density-ratio factor in the backward recursion by a sum over continuous and atomic histories.
seed_details.destination_search: The 2026 trajectory paper retains piecewise invertibility and explicitly excludes thresholds; no repeated-clamp mixed-history rate was found.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a routine iteration of the point-treatment decomposition.
seed_details.rebuttal: Atom masses and point regressions couple across histories, but the combinatorial recursion makes feasibility much lower than the one-time-point kernel and obscures the early-kill Gram question.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed identifies the first changed recursive proof step and is deferred rather than presented as a routine longitudinal extension.
